body.p: Claims 1-38 and 40-64 are pending in the application. Claims 43-64 have been added herein. No new matter has been added to the claims.

Claims 1-42 were rejected on the ground of non-statutory double patenting over claims 1- 35 of U.S. Patent No. 11,449,021 in view of U.S. Publication No. 2015/0336271 (hereinafter "Spicer"). Applicant canceled claim 39 (see responses filed on September 15, 2023 and March 21, 2024) and thus form PTOL-326 of the Non-Final Office Action dated June 6, 2024 stated claims 1-38 and 40-42 are pending. Therefore, claim 39 should not be included in the Office Actions non-statutory double patenting rejection. Additionally, Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

Applicant's amended features within claims 1, 20, 41 and 42 are not claimed within any claim of U.S. Patent No. 11,449,021 or disclosed within Spicer. Moreover, the claims of U.S. Publication No. 2015/0336271 and the disclosure of Spicer fail to disclose or suggest the features of each of claims 1, 20, 41 and 42 as a whole, and in particular at least the amended features within claims 1, 20, 41 and 42. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the non-statutory double patenting of claims 1-42 be withdrawn.
Claims 1-8, 10-38 and 40-42 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over U.S. Publication No. 2015/0336271 (hereinafter "Spicer") in view of U.S. Publication No. 2017/0095930 (hereinafter "Warashina").
Claim 9 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over Spicer in view of Warashina and further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2018/0345483 (hereinafter "Sirkett").

Claim 1 recites a method of robotic assembly comprising measuring a first feature of a first subcomponent; fitting the first feature to a corresponding feature of a model of the first subcomponent; determining a fixture location of the first subcomponent based on the fitting; receiving a first target location indicating where a first robot is to position the fixture location of the first subcomponent, the first target location proximal to a second target location indicating where a second robot is to position a second feature of a second subcomponent such that the first subcomponent and the second subcomponent form a component when coupled together with the fixture location of the first subcomponent in the first target location and the second feature of the second subcomponent in the second target location; calculating a first calculated location of the fixture location; measuring a first measured location of the fixture location; determining a first transformation matrix between the first calculated location and the first measured location; and repositioning the fixture location to the first target location using the first robot, the repositioning based on the first transformation matrix.

Neither Spicer or Warashina, singularly or in combination, disclose or suggest the features of claim 1 as a whole, and in particular at least the features of measuring a first feature of a first subcomponent; fitting the first feature to a corresponding feature of a model of the first subcomponent; determining a fixture location of the first subcomponent based on the fitting; receiving a first target location indicating where a first robot is to position the fixture location of the first subcomponent, the first target location proximal to a second target location indicating where a second robot is to position a second feature of a second subcomponent such that the first subcomponent and the second subcomponent form a component when coupled together with the fixture location of the first subcomponent in the first target location and the second feature of the second subcomponent in the second target location; calculating a first calculated location of the fixture location; measuring a first measured location of the fixture location; determining a first transformation matrix between the first calculated location and the first measured location; and repositioning the fixture location to the first target location using the first robot, the repositioning based on the first transformation matrix.

Neither Spicer or Warashina, singularly or in combination, disclose or suggest the features of claim 20 as a whole, and in particular at least the features of a first subcomponent comprising a first feature; a first robot; a second robot; and a control unit coupled to the first robot and the second robot, wherein the control unit includes a processor configured to measure the first feature, fit the first feature to a corresponding feature of a model of the first subcomponent, determine a fixture location on the first subcomponent based on the fit of the first feature to the corresponding feature, receive a first target location indicating where the first robot is to position the fixture location of the first subcomponent, the first target location proximal to a second target location indicating where the second robot is to position a second feature of a second subcomponent such that the first subcomponent and the second subcomponent form a component when coupled together with the fixture location of the first subcomponent in the first target location and the second feature of the second subcomponent in the second target location, calculate a first calculated location of the fixture location, measure a first measured location of the fixture location, determine a first transformation matrix between the first calculated location and the first measured
location, and reposition the fixture location to the first target location using the first robot, the repositioning based on the first transformation matrix.
